title: Open restriction of the dualizing product-square exchange
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient conventions [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $A=A_{E,n}$, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the constructible exceptional adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility]. For $Z=X,Y$, let $a_Z:Z\to s$ be the structure map, let $p_{1,Z},p_{2,Z}:Z\times_s Z\to Z$ be the projections, and put $\omega_Z=a_Z^!A_s\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, the dualizing object for every separated finite-type $Z$ of [def-fix-six-functor-datum](5); the constructible exceptional functor preserves this category by [def-trf-admissibility]. For every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], use an etale-origin representative as supplied by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], and let
$$B_{Z,M}=(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,a_Z,a_Z}(M))^{-1}:Rp_{1,Z!}p_{2,Z}^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}a_Z^*Ra_{Z!}M$$
use the normalized compact-support exchange of [def-exchange-projection], invertible on these bounded finite-Tor constructible inputs by [prop-functor-package](4), or [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] on their etale-origin representatives. In particular $M=\omega_Z$ is allowed. All the displayed maps are in the finite-coefficient constructible categories; no unrestricted ambient exceptional adjunction is asserted. Define $\chi_Z:p_{2,Z}^*\omega_Z\to p_{1,Z}^!A_Z$ to be the $Rp_{1,Z!}\dashv p_{1,Z}^!$ transpose of
$$a_Z^*(\varepsilon_{a_Z,A_s}^!)\circ B_{Z,\omega_Z}.$$
Write $J=j\times_s j$. Identify $j^!$ with $j^*$ and $J^!$ with $J^*$ as right adjoints of extension by zero, using the open adjunctions of [prop-exc-open-adjoint]. These open identifications and exceptional and pullback composition give
$$J^*p_{2,Y}^*\omega_Y\cong p_{2,X}^*\omega_X,\qquad J^*p_{1,Y}^!A_Y\cong p_{1,X}^!A_X,$$
where $j^*\omega_Y\cong j^!a_Y^!A_s\cong\omega_X$. Under these specific identifications, $J^*\chi_Y=\chi_X$. No properness of $X$ or $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(f), first sentence of the proof (locality of the product-square dualizing exchange), with projection indices interchanged; explicit finite-coefficient open-restriction formulation

proof.text: Use $\omega_Z$ for all separated finite-type $Z$ as defined in [def-fix-six-functor-datum](5), not a definition requiring properness. The constant unit $A_s$ has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$; the specified exceptional functors of [def-trf-admissibility] take it to $\omega_Z\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$. Pullbacks and compact-support images stay in the indicated finite-Tor constructible domains by [prop-functor-package] and [def-trf-admissibility]. Bounded constructible inputs have etale-origin representatives by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], so clause (4) of the package applies to $B_{Z,M}$ for every stated $M$, including $\omega_Z$. The adjunction of [prop-exc-open-adjoint] identifies $j^!$ with $j^*$ and every other open exceptional pullback with restriction. Exceptional composition therefore gives $j^*\omega_Y\simeq\omega_X$ and the endpoint identifications in the statement. The product corners are finite type over the Noetherian field spectrum, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every open in a Noetherian space is quasi-compact (the finite unions from a cover have a maximal member), so the corners are qcqs. The separated finite-type projections admit compactifications by [thm-nagata-compactification].

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(f), locality sentence; constructible finite-coefficient typing and open-composition identifications

proof.text:
Factor $J=u v$ through $W=X\times_sY$, where $u=j\times1_Y:W\hookrightarrow Y\times_sY$, $v=1_X\times j:X\times_sX\hookrightarrow W$, and write $r:W\to X$, $q:W\to Y$. The square $(u,r;p_{1,Y},j)$ is Cartesian; the square with top $J$ and bottom $j$ is generally not. Put $e_Y=\varepsilon_{a_Y,A_s}^!$ and $t_Y=a_Y^*e_Y\circ B_{Y,\omega_Y}$. Let $\delta_M:j^*Rp_{1,Y!}p_{2,Y}^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_!q^*M$ be compact-support exchange. The inverse exchange for the rectangle is
$$B^r_M:Rr_!q^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}a_X^*Ra_{Y!}M.$$
Apply the horizontal pasting equation of [fix-lem-exchanges](2) to base change of $a_Y$ first along $a_Y$ and then along $j$. With the maps normalized by [def-exchange-projection], it gives
$$B^r_M=j^*B_{Y,M}\circ\delta_M^{-1}.$$
Both sides are maps over $X$. Invertibility is [prop-functor-package](4); nothing here asserts $B^r_{\omega_Y}=B_{X,\omega_X}$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(f), locality reduction before (4.7); first product factor restricted

proof.text:
Set $\alpha=u^*\chi_Y:q^*\omega_Y\to r^!A_X$, using exceptional composition for $p_{1,Y}u=jr$. Its $Rr_!\dashv r^!$ adjunct is
$$t_r=j^*t_Y\circ\delta_{\omega_Y}^{-1}=a_X^*e_Y\circ B^r_{\omega_Y}.$$
To check the actual comparison, use the Hom bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_W(H,u^*p_{1,Y}^!A_Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y\times Y}(u_!H,p_{1,Y}^!A_Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rp_{1,Y!}u_!H,A_Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(j_!Rr_!H,A_Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(Rr_!H,j^*A_Y).$$
Take $H=q^*\omega_Y$. The first adjunct of $u^*\chi_Y$ is $\chi_Y\circ\varepsilon_u$ by naturality of the open counit. Apply [lem-amb-shriek-open-exchange-adjoint] on etale representatives with its $f=p_{1,Y}$, base open $j$ and source open $u$: it states exactly that the adjunct of $Rp_{1,Y!}\varepsilon_u$, after compact-support composition, is $\delta^{-1}$. Its Noetherian and compactification hypotheses were verified in Step 1. The equation of [lem-amb-compact-support-site-comparison-open] transports this specified inverse exchange and the open evaluation counits to our pro-etale representatives. Consequently the displayed Hom chain sends $\alpha$ to $j^*t_Y\circ\delta^{-1}$. These are the composite Hom bijections of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], with the exceptional comparison normalized as in [def-trf-admissibility].

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(f), exceptional-adjoint argument of diagram (4.7); explicit open-adjunction calculation

proof.text:
Put $N=j^*\omega_Y\simeq\omega_X$ and $c=\varepsilon_{j,\omega_Y}:j_!N\to\omega_Y$. The open base-change isomorphism of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] for the Cartesian square $(v,p_{2,X};q,j)$ is
$$\beta_N:q^*j_!N\xrightarrow{\sim}v_!p_{2,X}^*N.$$
It has its specified open-unit normalization. Consequently
$$q^*c\circ\beta_N^{-1}=\varepsilon_{v,q^*\omega_Y}:v_!v^*q^*\omega_Y\to q^*\omega_Y.$$
Indeed, transpose both sides by $v_!\dashv v^*$: the first becomes $v^*q^*\varepsilon_j$ composed with the pulled-back open unit, hence the identity by the triangle identity; the second is the identity by definition of the counit. The adjunction is [prop-exc-open-adjoint]. Since $j_!N$ is finite-Tor constructible by [lem-trf-open-ctf], all subsequent occurrences of $B^r_{j_!N}$ lie in the domain fixed in Step 1.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(f), locality sentence; second product factor, open base change and its counit normalization

proof.text:
Use naturality and vertical pasting in [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(2) for $a_X=a_Yj$. Under $Ra_{X!}\simeq Ra_{Y!}j_!$ and $Rp_{1,X!}\simeq Rr_!v_!$, their inverse-exchange equations are
$$B^r_{\omega_Y}\circ Rr_!q^*c=a_X^*Ra_{Y!}c\circ B^r_{j_!N},$$
$$B^r_{j_!N}\circ Rr_!(\beta_N^{-1})=B_{X,N}.$$
The first is naturality evaluated at the particular morphism $c:j_!N\to\omega_Y$. The second is the inverse of the vertical pasting equation for the square of $a_Y$ over $a_X$, with the square of $j$ over $q$ above it: the composite square is $a_X$ over itself. Its open-exchange component is precisely $\beta_N$ by [def-exchange-projection] and [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Substituting the equality from Step 4 gives the well-typed identity
$$B^r_{\omega_Y}\circ Rr_!\varepsilon_{v,q^*\omega_Y}=a_X^*Ra_{Y!}c\circ B_{X,N}.$$
It is an equality of maps $Rp_{1,X!}p_{2,X}^*N\to a_X^*Ra_{Y!}\omega_Y$ on $X$, with the displayed compact-support composition comparisons inserted.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(f), diagram (4.7), inverse compact-support exchange and the pasted square

proof.text:
The structural counits obey
$$e_X=e_Y\circ Ra_{Y!}c:Ra_{X!}\omega_X\simeq Ra_{Y!}j_!N\to A_s.$$
This is the composite-counit formula $\varepsilon_2\circ H\varepsilon_1$ of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], with $F=j_!$, $G=j^*$, $H=Ra_{Y!}$, $I=a_Y^!$, evaluated at $A_s$. The exceptional composition in [def-trf-admissibility] is specified as the conjugate of compact-support composition, so this is the actual $a_X$ counit under $N\simeq\omega_X$, not a counit chosen afterwards. This does not identify a pullback of $e_Y$ with $e_X$: both $e_Y$ and $e_X$ live over $s$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(f), right part of diagram (4.7); structural exceptional counits

proof.text:
The map $v^*\alpha=J^*\chi_Y$ has source $p_{2,X}^*N$ and target $p_{1,X}^!A_X$. Under the composite adjunction $Rr_!v_!\dashv v^*r^!$ its adjunct is
$$t_r\circ Rr_!\varepsilon_{v,q^*\omega_Y}.$$
This follows immediately by applying the composite Hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] first to the open restriction $v^*\alpha$ and then to $\alpha$: the first adjunct is $\alpha\circ\varepsilon_v$. By Steps 3, 5 and 6 the displayed composite equals
$$a_X^*e_Y\circ a_X^*Ra_{Y!}c\circ B_{X,N}=a_X^*e_X\circ B_{X,\omega_X}.$$
The latter is the defining adjunct of $\chi_X$. The adjunction of [def-trf-admissibility] is a Hom bijection, so its injectivity proves $J^*\chi_Y=\chi_X$ under exactly the open and composition identifications in the statement.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(f), conclusion by exceptional adjointness after diagram (4.7)

The delivery has no new nodes and I made no changes. Statement: replacing the proper-only def-trf-dualizing-complex with def-fix-six-functor-datum(5), and quantifying M in D^b_ctf, are recorded in the report. They add no hypothesis, the conclusion is unchanged, and both citers are unaffected. The new factorisation J=u∘v through W=X×Y is right: I checked that both squares are Cartesian, and the two-point example confirms the old square was not. Each step checked by hand. Step 2: horizontal pasting gives B^r=j^*B_Y∘δ^{-1}. Step 3: lem-amb-shriek-open-exchange-adjoint with f=p1Y, the base open j and the source open u gives the adjunct j^*t_Y∘C^{-1}, and the Hom chain is the conjugate of compact-support composition. Step 4: the triangle identity gives q^*c∘β^{-1}=ε_v. Step 5: vertical pasting with the composite square a_X over a_X (legs rv=p1X and p2X) gives B_X,N=B^r_{j_!N}∘Rr_!β^{-1}. Step 6: the composite counit gives e_X=e_Y∘Ra_Y!c. Step 7: by adjunction injectivity, J^*χ_Y=χ_X. Hypotheses: Noetherian corners via the Mathlib leaf; compactifiability via Nagata; D^+ étale-origin witnesses for transport and invertibility; j_!N in D^b_ctf via lem-trf-open-ctf. One detail is left implicit: that the composition comparisons are compatible with the étale→pro-étale transport. That comes from the transported package, so I do not count it as a gap. The graph is acyclic and every cited id exists and is unmerged. The dualizing-exchange duplicate search over dag/nodes and blueprint_refs found nothing. I accept all eight declared tool_uses; only lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization and lem-trf-open-ctf are off-route, and both are generic tools. No SGA source is used. Details are in review.md.
